explanation: When Queen Victoria chose to sing 'Italien' for Felix, he confessed that Fanny had written it. Fanny later published music under her own name.

claims.text: Felix Mendelssohn published several songs by his sister Fanny under his own name.
Robert Schumann, Franz Liszt and Johannes Brahms did not publish songs by a sister named Fanny under their own names.
Queen Victoria sang Fanny Mendelssohn's song Italien to Felix, who told her that his sister had written it.
Fanny Mendelssohn later published music under her own name.

evidence.restatement: Felix Mendelssohn put songs by his sister Fanny into his own published sets (Op. 8 and Op. 9).
Schumann, Liszt and Brahms did not publish a sister Fanny's songs as their own.
When Queen Victoria sang Italien for Felix in 1842, he admitted that Fanny had composed it.
Fanny later published music under her own name (from 1846).
Felix Mendelssohn published six of Fanny's songs under his own name, in his Opp. 8 and 9.
No such story attaches to Schumann, Liszt or Brahms.
Queen Victoria asked for Italien, and Felix admitted that Fanny had composed it.
Fanny began publishing under her own name in 1846, shortly before her death.
